findings.description: `pup ui`'s doc claim "Piped or redirected, it prints what `pup status` prints" is now false outside a repo: `pup status` unconditionally prints the fleet view there (decision 60), while `pup ui` still auto-selects the sole project via the unchanged `project()`/decision-43 path and prints the single-project table.
findings.body:
This sentence predates PR #106 and wasn't revisited when `pup status`'s outside-a-repo behavior changed.

- `pup status` (bare, no `--project`) outside any repo now **always** prints the fleet view (`printFleet`), even with exactly one registered project — see `src/cli/index.ts` lines 901-923 and the test `'is the view outside a repo even with only one project registered'` in `src/cli/index.test.ts`.
- `pup ui` still resolves through the unmodified `project()` helper (decision 43's single-project auto-select), and when piped/non-TTY calls `printDashboard(db, read())` — the single-project full table, never `printFleet` (`src/cli/index.ts` lines 926-937).

So outside a repo with exactly one registered project, piped `pup ui` and typed `pup status` now print two different shapes, contradicting the doc's unqualified claim.

Suggested fix:
```markdown
  Piped or redirected inside a repo, it prints what `pup status` prints there, once, and
  exits 0; outside a repo `pup ui` still resolves through decision 43's single-project rule,
  not the fleet `pup status` prints there — it has no fleet view yet (decision 60).
```

<https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/2d766b59b46782c0192b031b758b76c868caa817/docs/02-cli.md#L72-L78>

findings.description: The pre-existing JSDoc explaining why `pup status` and `pup ui` share one snapshot-reading function (decision 52) used to sit directly above `printDashboard`; this diff inserted `printFleet` and its own JSDoc between them without relocating it, so the old comment now hovers over `printFleet` (which it doesn't describe) and `printDashboard` is left with no docstring.

`fleetProjects(base?: string)`'s `base` parameter has no caller — production and both test call sites always invoke it with zero arguments — so per this repo's Altitude/YAGNI rule it should be inlined to `fleetProjects()` until a second caller or a stated WHY justifies it.

`fleetSummary`'s `needsYou` filter re-derives the "blocked or stalled" condition inline instead of reusing the existing private `sortsFirst` helper in the same file, which is exactly that condition; could be `sortsFirst(session) || session.state === 'awaiting-review'` to keep the classification defined once.

The addendum's bolded lead sentence and decision 60's echo both state in the present tense that "`pup status` and `pup ui` may read across stores," before the immediately-following text clarifies `pup ui --all` doesn't exist yet — a reader skimming just the bold claim could conclude `pup ui --all` is already implemented.

"Dormant projects are hidden unless `--dormant` is given, per the design" cites no concrete decision or design doc — `dormant`/`--dormant` appears nowhere else in the repo's design docs or decision history, breaking this file's otherwise careful citation discipline.

The comment justifying why `state` isn't sanitized ("checked on write") overstates the guarantee — `sessions.state` has no SQL CHECK constraint and a session with direct SQLite access could write arbitrary bytes there; what actually makes printing raw `state` safe on the fleet path is `fleetSummary`'s strict-equality filter against known enum literals, not a write-time check.

`paths.eventsFile(row.id)` uses raw session-writable `row.id` as a path segment with no traversal check; this PR's fleet view now exercises this against every registered project's store rather than only the caller's own, widening the pre-existing issue's blast radius without introducing it.

A `Notification` hook's `event.message` flows unsanitized into `SessionActivity.detail` and is rendered raw by `activityLabel`'s awaiting-input branch on the single-project table; not reachable through the new fleet view (its needsYou filter excludes plain awaiting-input sessions), and not touched by this PR.
